Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details. TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx FINANCIAL AID Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units. EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration TEST CREDIT If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit TRANSFER HELP Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors! Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4 Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu You are also welcome to visit us in person. TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: CONCENTRATIONS Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations: Creative Writing Linguistics Literature Rhetoric and Writing Studies Self-Directed Study MAJOR INFORMATION The B.A. in English at CSUSB integrates four distinct approaches that are rarely united in English programs: literary studies, creative writing, linguistics, and rhetoric/writing studies. Students in our program gain an in-depth understanding of the imaginative, discursive, and practical aspects of language, as they read, interpret, synthesize, and write texts of various kinds. With this background, our graduates are prepared for careers in writing, business, public relations, advertising, technology, public health, teaching, and many other fields. They can also pursue graduate studies in a wide variety of disciplines, including law and medicine. Additionally, our graduates will find themselves well-prepared to take on the responsibilities of civic and community engagement. Students interested in the Self-Directed Study Concentration must write a proposal for their program plan, including all of the courses that they intend to take in the concentration and a rationale for the course of study. The proposal will be vetted by an English faculty committee before a student can be approved for this concentration. Before declaring this concentration, a student must have completed several core classes, which are listed in the catalog. The Minor in English Teacher Preparation provides students planning to pursue a single subject credential in English with supplemental training in this subject area. The Minor in Speech-Language Pathology allows students to complete the required coursework to be eligible to apply to most Master's degrees in Speech-Language Pathology and Communication Sciences and Disorders and eventually obtain employment in that field. ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/english/english-ba/ CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS Find out more about this major here: What is the English Major? ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) All concentrations in this major are similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in English EXCEPT for the Self-Directed Study Concentration. HOWEVER, the articulation agreement below represents the straightest pathway through the major. Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met. Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.

CONCENTRATIONS

Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations:

  • Creative Writing
  • Linguistics
  • Literature
  • Rhetoric and Writing Studies
  • Self-Directed Study


MAJOR INFORMATION

The B.A. in English at CSUSB integrates four distinct approaches that are rarely united in English programs: literary studies, creative writing, linguistics, and rhetoric/writing studies. Students in our program gain an in-depth understanding of the imaginative, discursive, and practical aspects of language, as they read, interpret, synthesize, and write texts of various kinds. With this background, our graduates are prepared for careers in writing, business, public relations, advertising, technology, public health, teaching, and many other fields. They can also pursue graduate studies in a wide variety of disciplines, including law and medicine. Additionally, our graduates will find themselves well-prepared to take on the responsibilities of civic and community engagement.


Students interested in the Self-Directed Study Concentration must write a proposal for their program plan, including all of the courses that they intend to take in the concentration and a rationale for the course of study. The proposal will be vetted by an English faculty committee before a student can be approved for this concentration. Before declaring this concentration, a student must have completed several core classes, which are listed in the catalog.


The Minor in English Teacher Preparation provides students planning to pursue a single subject credential in English with supplemental training in this subject area. The Minor in Speech-Language Pathology allows students to complete the required coursework to be eligible to apply to most Master's degrees in Speech-Language Pathology and Communication Sciences and Disorders and eventually obtain employment in that field.


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/english/english-ba/


CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS

Find out more about this major here:

  • What is the English Major?


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

All concentrations in this major are similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in English EXCEPT for the Self-Directed Study Concentration.

HOWEVER, the articulation agreement below represents the straightest pathway through the major.


Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
